body: Quick pass: touched suites green on the final head 765fadb80 - mcp_live ui_link 7 passed (including the false-window pin: no tool call reaches a peer that does not prove the token), app lib 307, clippy app clean. No visible UI change, so no screenshots apply. Backward compatible: an old CLI's nonce-less hello still gets plain HELLO_OK. Ready for review.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 765fadb802a6c733aa60cb6362424c63d8ae0a75 -->
Needs changes before merge.

I read the complete six-file diff and issue #3874. This is the first review of this head.

What looks good:
- The client removes entries when the OS reports a dead process.
- The server keeps the reply format for clients that send no nonce.
- The added test checks that a plain HELLO_OK receives no tool call.

Local review results:
- Trial merge with upstream/main 707dac12a85f9744640ef2f682fd5653f1fa83b9: clean.
- Local merge: ffb0f0390a92fb8cf15007edbbbbaf5007715465. Its first parent is the full PR head above.
- Laws checked against upstream/main:AGENTS.md.
- Not built: needs a maintainer look at crates/app/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock first. The PR adds direct libc and windows-sys dependencies. Both already occur in the lockfile, but these are new dependency declarations. PR-reviewer hard rules prohibit a build for this change.
- Quick gate, light lane, app tests, and clippy: not run. The author's recorded results are not independent review results.
- Extra suites run: none. The diff changes no fixture directory, importer, post, operation, motion code, or catalog.
- Safety tier: no. The diff changes MCP transport code. No posted G-code, collision check, stock simulation, or geometry changes occur.
- Mutations: none. No Cargo command ran.
- Goldens moved: none. No crates/ui change occurs, so screenshots do not apply.

Requested before merge:

1. BLOCKER: crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:153 and crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:142. The hello sends both the token and nonce before the server proves its identity. A false server can read these fields and calculate the exact token_proof reply. It needs no discovery-file access. A stale entry whose PID was reused, or whose liveness is unknown, still reaches this path. The added test only checks a server that sends no proof. Use an authentication exchange that proves prior knowledge of the secret without disclosing it first, or use a transport that verifies the peer identity. Add a false-server test that computes its reply from the received hello and still receives no tool call.

2. BLOCKER: crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:147-156. HELLO_TIMEOUT is a socket read timeout, not a deadline for the whole exchange. Each successful read permits another read with the full timeout. A peer can send one byte every four seconds and keep the client waiting far beyond five seconds. The new 1 MiB allowance makes this wait much longer. Track one elapsed-time deadline through the exchange. Add a slow-input test that ends within that deadline.

3. BLOCKER: crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:322-329. take(MAX_ANSWER) ends a read even without a newline. The next loop creates a new limit and treats the remainder as another line. An oversized JSON answer is ignored in pieces. With the socket still open and no read timeout, the client can then wait indefinitely. A peer can also place a valid reply in a later piece of the same oversized line. Refuse the connection when a line reaches the limit without its delimiter. Add tests for oversized input with and without a final newline. Do not parse a remainder as a new message.

4. BLOCKER: crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:364-369. When the bridge reaches MAX_BRIDGE, it returns Ok even if the peer has more output. This reports success after a truncated MCP response and can end a valid long session midway through a message. Return a visible failure when the size limit ends the transfer. Add a bridge test that exceeds the bound and checks the error and exit status.

The dependency decision remains necessary after these changes. Keep the contributor's ready/draft state unchanged. The review worktree and review-3971 branch remain in place as requested.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed (review 765fadb802a6c733aa60cb6362424c63d8ae0a75). One commit closes the four findings; the new head waits for a fresh review.

1. Transport redesign (docs/decisions/3874-ui-link-transport.md): the link no longer sends the token to a peer that has proved nothing.
   - Windows: the window listens on a named pipe `\\.\pipe\camcraft-ui-link-<pid>` with a user-only ACL. The CLI asks the kernel which process serves the pipe (`GetNamedPipeServerProcessId`) and refuses a peer that is not the process the file names. This runs before the hello: a false server never sees the token.
   - Unix keeps the 0700 socket folder, per the reviewer's read of the issue: the risk does not occur there.
   - A `"tcp"` entry is refused by name on every platform, with the risk in the diagnostic.
   - The nonce/proof exchange is removed: it disclosed the token to the very peer it tried to check.
   - Pinned: `a_pipe_served_by_another_process_gets_no_token_and_no_tool_call` (the false server could compute any reply from what it receives - it receives nothing), and `a_tcp_link_file_is_refused_by_name`.
2. One elapsed deadline now covers the connect, the hello write and the answer read. A peer that trickles one byte at a time ends within it. Pinned: `a_slow_peer_ends_within_the_hello_deadline`.
3. A line that reaches the 1 MiB bound without its newline closes the link. No remainder of an oversized line is read as a new message, so a valid reply hidden after it never counts. Pinned with and without a final newline: `an_answer_line_past_the_bound_is_refused_and_never_split`.
4. The bridge bound is a visible failure now: one probe byte past the bound says whether the session was still open, and a truncated answer reports the bound and exit 1. Pinned: `the_bridge_reports_a_truncated_session_at_its_bound`.

Dependency note for the maintainer: the direct dependency declarations stay for your decision. `windows-sys` on Windows (already in the lock, no new crate): the pid-alive check and now the named-pipe transport itself - std has no pipe API. The feature list grows by `Win32_System_Pipes`, `Win32_System_IO`, `Win32_Storage_FileSystem`, `Win32_Security`, `Win32_Security_Authorization`. `libc` on Unix stays for the pid check. Please confirm these declarations.

Gate on the final head: `mcp_live ui_link` 11 passed, `mcp_live` full binary 25 passed, app lib 307 passed, clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Per #3727 the PR keeps its ready flag while the findings are fixed; nothing was pushed after the review except this commit.

Labels set: needs-maintainer + conflicts (needs-rework removed).

- `needs-maintainer`: the review could not build this PR and the PR declares two new dependency declarations (`libc` on Unix, `windows-sys` on Windows, in `crates/app/Cargo.toml`) that the maintainer has not yet confirmed. `gh pr edit` fails on this repo; the labels were set through the REST API.
- `conflicts`: the PR does not merge with `main` - it conflicts in `link.rs`, `link_client.rs`, `listen.rs` and `ui_link.rs`, because main merged PR #3883 (a different fix for the same issue #3874) at 2026-11-25T05:41Z. No local resolution is safe; the maintainer picks a design or the author refreshes and reconciles. This is a fork PR, so its draft state is untouched.

Closing as superseded by the merged #3883, whose mutual siphash proof keeps the raw token off the wire. The named-pipe transport with kernel-verified server identity, the pid-alive stale-file check, and the two incidental bug fixes stay preserved on this branch for follow-up #3995 - the maintainer can reopen or take them from there.
